root_idea.summary: The root centers on pleasantness, savoring, and what is experienced as agreeable or enjoyable.
root_idea.development: From this orientation it extends to fruit as something relished, cheerfulness and pleasant conversation, and certain specialized descriptions of especially good milk. The Quranic expression تَفَكَّهُونَ in 56:65 is disputed in the lexical tradition: it is variously connected with fruit-taking, banter, wonder, or regret, while one analysis treats it as related to تَفَكَّنُونَ through substitution.

senses.definition: Fruit; something whose eating is enjoyed.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun is used for fruit generally, including fruit described alongside dates and pomegranates; the lexical evidence records discussion over the scope of that category.
Used of people enjoying what has been granted to them and living in agreeable abundance.

senses.definition: To be amused or to wonder at what has happened.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative interpretation associated with the Quranic plural in 36:55; the supplied evidence preserves the interpretation without treating a variant vocalization as a separate Quran location.

senses.definition: Jocose, cheerful, or given to jesting.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural at 83:31 is understood in the sense of jesting or light-hearted amusement.

senses.definition: Exulting greatly, sometimes with insolence or ingratitude.
senses.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported for a short-vowel Quranic plural reading in the lexical evidence; no additional modern verse location is claimed for that reading.

In the Quranic expression of 56:65, this fruit-related sense is also explained ironically as making fruit the subject of one's speech; the same discussion records explanations involving taking up fruit.

senses.definition: To discard or abstain from fruit.
senses.usage_conditions: A contrary fruit-related interpretation reported in the discussion of 56:65; it is preserved as a lexical alternative rather than generalized as the ordinary meaning of the verb.

senses.definition: To engage in pleasant talk or banter.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic interpretation of 56:65, this is understood as engaging in فُكَاهَة, while the same construction can more generally describe amusement through conversation.

senses.definition: To wonder at or be astonished by what has happened.
senses.usage_conditions: One explicit interpretation of the Quranic expression in 56:65.

senses.definition: To repent, grieve, lament, or regret.
senses.usage_conditions: Another explicit interpretation of the Quranic expression in 56:65; one root-level analysis connects this interpretation with a substituted form related to تَفَكَّنُونَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cheerful, happy, or free from constraint; to be jocose and given to laughter, including making one's companions laugh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use describing a cheerful or joking disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To entertain people with novel or facetious sayings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II causative use involving amusing conversation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To jest or joke with someone and indulge in pleasantry with them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III reciprocal or interpersonal construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel: to yield milk plentifully in connection with eating spring herbage before parturition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV use; related descriptions mention laxity near parturition and enlargement of the udder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who eats fruit, or is characterized by eating fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive epithet applied to a person, distinct from the adjective meaning cheerful or jocose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To amuse oneself with conversation or affect joking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form V use modeled on the enjoyment of fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak evil of someone in their absence and defame them while jesting with others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with the construction تَفَكَّهَ بِفُلَانٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual jesting or joking among several people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI verbal noun and its corresponding reciprocal use.
A substantive noun for pleasantry, distinguished from the Form I infinitive in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possessing fruit, or having fruit in abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet comparable to other possessive formations; it can describe one whose fruit has become plentiful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm tree that inspires admiration, pleasure, or joy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized use, apparently associated with the tree's abundant fruit.
A comparative figurative extension of the fruit term.
A relational noun formed from فَاكِهَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wonderful or astonishing thing, including a remarkable saying or story.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of something that provokes wonder or admiration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose milk is thick like colostrum or flows plentifully around parturition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial noun; descriptions also connect it with abundant milk before giving birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who delights in speaking evil of people, especially in their absence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized interpersonal use describing pleasure in malicious talk; distinct from ordinary cheerfulness or joking.

cautions: The interpretations of تَفَكَّهُونَ in 56:65 are genuinely divided among fruit-taking, fruit-abstention, banter, wonder, and regret; the entry preserves these as distinct Quran-attested alternatives rather than treating the contextual English gloss as decisive.

The evidence reports Quranic readings and interpretations with differing vocalizations for فَاكِهِينَ and فَكِهِينَ. The cited historical reference for the short-vowel exultation reading is not converted into an additional modern verse location.
Some Classical meanings are specialized or figurative extensions of the fruit and pleasantness vocabulary and should not be assumed for every Quran occurrence.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane report connecting the short-vowel plural فَكِهِينَ with a Quranic reading cannot be securely matched to a separate supplied QAC occurrence and modern location; its lexical content is retained under فَكِهٌ as a variant Quran-attested sense without assigning an invented verse key.
